content:
Camila Reyes: Hey all — quick ask for a cross-functional fact-check pass on the first wave of customer stories before we send drafts to customers for approval. Looking for 4–6 volunteers from PM / SE / Support to sanity-check technical claims + anything that could get us in trouble (overstated metrics, security language, etc.).

Camila Reyes: Drafts in progress:
- Northwind (Dedicated + routing/fallback + caching)
- Helios (Private/VPC + audit logs/KMS + compliance-safe wording)
- Atlas (RAG + eval harness + migration story)

Camila Reyes: What we need reviewed:
1) Are the product capabilities described accurately (what’s GA vs “available” vs roadmap)?
2) Any claims that require proof we don’t have (p95 latency, $/1M tokens, uptime)?
3) Any “gotcha” language (esp. security/compliance) we should soften.
4) Diagram correctness (if you’re SE-minded :))

Camila Reyes: If you can help, reply with which story you want + how much time you can give (30 min is fine). Goal is comments by EOD Mon so we stay on the week 7–9 approvals timeline. :pray:

Soojin Lee: +1 to this. Please be ruthless on wording like “guarantee,” “always,” “no downtime,” etc. We should keep it to approved pillars + proof requirements. If you spot a sentence that needs a citation, just tag it “PROOF?” and we’ll route.

Ethan Wallace: I’ll take Northwind for a first read (tone + claims). If someone can validate the Dedicated sizing / routing bits, that’d be huge. I’m in for ~45 mins today.

Markus Klein: I can cover the Dedicated technical accuracy for Northwind (routing/fallback policies, caching/batching language). 30–45 min. Drop me the latest link.

Camila Reyes: Thanks Markus. Latest doc links here (internal):
- Northwind draft: https://drive.google.com/…/northwind-draft
- Helios draft: https://drive.google.com/…/helios-draft
- Atlas outline: https://drive.google.com/…/atlas-outline

Camila Reyes: (also, if you prefer reviewing in the docs PR format, DevEx has the template wired up — but Google Doc comments are easiest right now.)

Simran Kaur: I can review the architecture diagrams + any mentions of “KV cache / continuous batching / fallback routing” to make sure it’s not hand-wavy. I’ll do Northwind diagram + a quick skim of Helios.

Rachel Kim: I can do a sensitivity pass from CS angle (what might make a customer uncomfortable, anything that conflicts w/ current escalations, and what’s safe to say publicly). I’ll take Helios + Atlas.

Miguel Santos: I’ll help on Atlas. Mainly will check the migration claims + any references to competitor comparisons. 30 min.

Tyler Benson: I can track reviewers + status. If folks drop comments by Mon, I’ll consolidate into a checklist + update the exec weekly readout. Also happy to set up a lightweight “claims log” if that helps.

Alex Chen: Support volunteer here — I can spot-check any reliability statements and make sure we’re not contradicting known incident history (e.g., “no latency spikes” type claims). I’ll focus on Northwind since that one’s most likely to get challenged by prospects.

Priya Nair: PM volunteer — I can review Helios language around audit logs / retention / KMS integrations to ensure it matches what’s actually shipped vs configurable per deployment. 30 min.

Soojin Lee: Thank you all. Quick reminder: if you see a metric, please also comment whether it should be an exact number vs a range (Legal has been pushing ranges unless we have a clean methodology + customer sign-off).

Markus Klein: Skimming now. First thing: the Northwind draft says “automatic fallback to a secondary model in all regions.” That’s not true as written — fallback depends on the policy + what models are enabled in that region/capacity tier. I’ll leave a suggested rewrite in-doc.

Ethan Wallace: Good catch. I’ll adjust copy to “policy-based fallback to compatible model variants/regions (when configured)” and avoid “all regions.”

Simran Kaur: Diagram note: current Northwind diagram shows “Optimizer” inline on request path. Optimize isn’t a runtime service in-line; it’s recommendations + config tooling. Suggest we represent it as “Console/Optimize (ops)” sidecar, not a hop.

Camila Reyes: Yep, we should not imply Optimize is a mandatory on-path component. Please mark it up and I’ll have Design update the block.

Alex Chen: Also flagging the sentence “p95 latency stable under peak load” w/o a window. Support-wise we’ve seen at least one transient spike during the interview window (resolved, but still). Recommend “p95 latency remained within agreed SLO during the measured period” + add a footnote on measurement window.

Rachel Kim: On Helios: avoid “HIPAA-compliant deployment” unless customer + Legal explicitly approve and we can back it (BAA, etc.). Safer: “designed to support regulated workloads” + mention audit logs/KMS/data residency requirements.

Priya Nair: +1 Rachel. I left comments on the exact phrasing. Also the draft says “customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM” — HSM is only for certain Private setups; we should scope it to “KMS integration; HSM support available for select deployments” or drop HSM.

Miguel Santos: Atlas outline has “cut inference cost by 60%” as a placeholder. We should label that clearly as “target / unverified” until metrics worksheet is filled + approved. I tagged it.

Tyler Benson: I’ll add a checklist section in the tracker: “Metric verified + approved for publish (Y/N)” and “Exact vs range.” If you want, react :white_check_mark: on your top-level comment when you’re done.

Soojin Lee: Amazing. When you leave comments, please also tag the owner:
- Messaging: @Soojin Lee
- Technical accuracy: @Markus Klein / @Simran Kaur
- CS sensitivity: @Rachel Kim
- Draft copy: @Ethan Wallace
- Program/logistics: @Camila Reyes

Camila Reyes: Closing the loop — thank you. Plan:
- Review comments through Mon EOD
- Tue: implement edits + run final claims/proof check
- Wed: send to customers w/ a 5 business day review window

Camila Reyes: If anyone else wants to help, jump in. Even 15 mins to scan for over-claims is valuable.
